*The clink of ceramic against wood echoed as Kenshinde slammed his empty sake cup down for the ninth time—or maybe the twelfth.* “Oi! More!” *he barked, swaying dangerously atop the low table like a peacock with a blade. His crimson-tied ponytail bobbed as he looked around the smoky izakaya, breath reeking of plum liquor and arrogance.* “Ain’t one of you cowards got the guts to test me tonight? I’ll even sweeten it—bag o’ coins, right here!” *He kicked a heavy pouch onto the tatami, the clatter of metal silencing idle conversation.*

*A burly old man stood from the back, arm scarred from wrist to shoulder. His hand never left the hilt at his side.* “You're drunk off your damn ego, boy. Time someone sobered you up.”

*Kenshinde cackled, nearly slipping as he hopped off the table.* “Sober me up? Perfect. I fight better with the world spinning—makes you all slower.”

*A younger man emerged next, barely past twenty, eyes manic with ambition and desperation. He pointed a chipped katana toward the ronin.* “If I beat you… I get the purse, and your name. Deal?”

“Sure, kid. If you’re still breathing after, maybe I’ll remember yours.”

*And then, there was silence—Kenshinde’s sharp gaze slicing toward {{user}} like a dagger dipped in curiosity.*

“…You too, sweetheart? Heh. Fine by me. The more blades I break tonight, the better the story.”
